works.title: Constitutional Amendment Satire: Originalist Misinterpretation
works.description: A satirical political piece examining how the contemporary right strategically reinterprets plainly worded constitutional amendments through false originalism. Focuses on the 13th Amendment and its 'punishment clause' as a mechanism for legal slavery reinstatement, contrasting stated originalist principles with actual practice of constitutional manipulation.
works.quote: I'm working on a satirical piece examining how the political right manages to reinterpret plainly worded constitutional amendments through originalist frameworks that contradict the actual original intent.

works.title: Romance: Heir and Professor
works.description: A romance novel centered on a young heir to a substantial family fortune who enrolls in graduate-level negotiation and finance coursework to prepare for managing the family empire. The story opens with a first kiss between the teenage heir and his college professor. Features power dynamics across age and status differences.
works.quote: As a young heir to a huge family fortune... I was impatient and didn't want to waste time in college... While still a teenager, I encountered my professor. To my surprise and delight, she replied, 'I would love to have lunch with you.'

works.title: Christian Nationalism Research Dossier
works.description: A comprehensive research dossier on Christian Nationalism structured in three parts: Part 1 is a Bible-fluency substrate grounding the theological claims of Christian nationalism (with scriptural citations and translations); Part 3 examines diagnostic literature (SBC resolutions, FRC statements, mega-church histories) to trace how the movement coordinates institutional capture. Includes deep research on prior theological traditions (Abraham Joshua Heschel, Jeremiah, etc.) that stand in opposition.
works.quote: For the Bible-fluency substrate (Part 1), which translation should anchor the full-text quotations? A: NIV (most-cited in modern Evangelicalism). For the diagnostic literature (Part 3), how deep should the documentary substrate go — SBC resolutions, FRC statements, Liberty/BJU histories, mega-church landscape?
